visitor_mode: Persuade with a tool entry point (an AI tool-stack recommender landing page); inferred from the h1 'Tell us the goal. We'll build the stack.' and the 'Find my stack' CTA.
overall_reason: The page has no photographs or captures; its one picture is the hero's right half, three floating HTML cards (goal, recommended stack, workflow) on an empty pale-blue gradient wash, which stands in for the recommender's real result screen.

score.reason: T-STAND-IN fails on the hero's styled-div result cards for a product that exists, and T-DELETE-PICTURE finds that the 544 by 384px gradient wash behind them carries nothing; T-ICON-SYSTEM passes on the two filled glyphs (IMG-005, IMG-003).

findings.where: hero right half, div.absolute.inset-x-6 and its three cards, 1440 (tiles/1440-00.png, contact sheet #1)
findings.evidence: The hero picture is three HTML cards: 'Your goal / Start a YouTube channel / Video, Under $25', 'Recommended stack / Perplexity, ElevenLabs, CapCut' and 'Workflow 1 to 3'. The imagery table records no img, svg or capture anywhere on the page (counts.images 0, content_pictures 0). The recommender exists behind the 'Find my stack' button, so its real result screen could have been captured.
findings.before: Three floating styled-div cards that mimic a result screen.
findings.after: A 2x capture of the real result screen for one goal (the YouTube channel stack with its prices and steps), labelled with the inputs that produced it.
findings.why: A drawn stand-in tells the visitor what the result might look like; a capture shows what the tool actually returns.

findings.where: hero, decoration div.absolute.inset-x-6 (544 by 384px at y 145), 1440 (contact sheet #1)
findings.evidence: The imagery table lists this as a large gradient field with no text: linear-gradient to right bottom in pale blue at 10% alpha. The three cards sit over and beyond its edges, and the wash itself shows nothing.
findings.before: An empty pale-blue gradient panel behind the cards.
findings.after: Remove the wash, or put the real result capture in that frame.
findings.why: Deleting the wash loses nothing; it is there to balance the split hero.

findings.where: tool directory cards and compare table, 1440 (shot-1440.png y 1390 to 2390)
findings.evidence: Six directory cards name real products (Claude, Perplexity, Canva, ElevenLabs, CapCut, Lovable) as text only, with no owner's mark, and the hero's 'Recommended stack' list marks each tool with a coloured dot.
findings.before: Tool names as plain text with coloured dots.
findings.after: Each owner's one-colour mark at one height (20px) beside its name in the directory cards.
findings.why: A visitor scanning a tool directory recognises marks faster than names; the coloured dots carry no meaning.

strengths: The hero cards use the tool's real vocabulary (a goal, a budget tag, three named tools and a three-step workflow), so as an illustration they read at their size (T-ILLUSTRATION-READ).
